key_insight: Agent-Guided Concept Discovery learns interpretable, diagnostically relevant concepts directly from REIMS data to improve surgical margin assessment without needing predefined concept labels.
engineering_relevance: The approach aims to make intraoperative mass-spectrometry models more clinically reliable by improving generalization under noisy operating-room conditions while keeping decisions explainable.
method: Learns concepts from unlabeled REIMS spectra instead of requiring concept annotations
Uses a reasoning agent to refine concept names/descriptions and reweight them by diagnostic relevance
Grounds learned concepts with a biochemical knowledge graph for metabolic consistency
evidence_signal: Across Skin and Breast Cancer datasets, the model improves balanced accuracy and sensitivity over the baseline, and a representative intraoperative case shows fewer false positives.
watch_item: Clinical deployment may still depend on the quality of the knowledge graph and how robustly the learned concepts transfer across hospitals, instruments, and surgical workflows.
paper_title: Agent-Guided Relational Concept Discovery: Toward Interpretable Surgical Margin Assessment
